research_question: In adults with renal (kidney) stones, what is the effect of extracorporeal shock wave lithotripsy (ESWL/SWL) compared with retrograde intrarenal surgery (RIRS, flexible ureteroscopy with laser lithotripsy) on treatment success (stone-free or clinically insignificant residual fragments on imaging) at approximately three months?
control_label: Retrograde intrarenal surgery (RIRS, flexible ureteroscopy with laser lithotripsy)
outcome_description: Number of participants treated successfully (stone-free, or free of clinically significant residual fragments per the trial's own definition, e.g. fully stone-free or residual fragments =4 mm, as assessed by CT, ultrasound or plain X-ray) out of the number randomised to each arm, at the approximately three-month follow-up. Where only another timepoint is reported (e.g. 1 or 6 months), the closest timepoint to three months is used and noted; percentages are converted to counts using the number analysed in that arm; reported failures/residual stone rates are converted to successes (total minus failures). Outcome reflects the full planned treatment course when multiple ESWL or RIRS sessions were permitted; number randomised is used as the denominator (intention-to-treat). In three-arm trials also including percutaneous nephrolithotomy (PCNL), only the ESWL and RIRS arms are extracted. Operating time, hospital stay, complications, re-treatment, pain, stone size reduction and quality of life are not pooled.
positive_direction: A positive effect (RR > 1) means a HIGHER treatment success (stone-free) rate with ESWL than with RIRS; RR < 1 means a lower success rate with ESWL, favouring RIRS.
search_queries: shock wave lithotripsy versus retrograde intrarenal surgery randomized trial kidney stones
ESWL vs flexible ureteroscopy laser lithotripsy stone-free rate renal calculi trial
SWL RIRS comparison stone free rate three months randomized controlled
inclusion_criteria: Randomised controlled trial in adults (=18 years) with renal/kidney stones comparing ESWL/SWL with RIRS (flexible ureteroscopy with laser lithotripsy), including three-arm trials that also include PCNL (ESWL and RIRS arms extracted only)
Reports a treatment success / stone-free (or clinically insignificant residual fragment) outcome at any follow-up time, with the timepoint closest to three months used

Provides quantitative data allowing computation of event counts per arm (counts, percentages with denominators, or failure counts convertible to successes); conference abstracts are eligible if they report these data
exclusion_criteria: Not an original empirical study (systematic review, meta-analysis, narrative review, editorial, opinion piece, commentary, or purely theoretical/modelling paper)
No comparison between an ESWL arm and an RIRS arm (e.g. single-arm series, ESWL vs PCNL only, or RIRS vs PCNL only)
No quantitative outcome data from which an effect size can be computed (no event counts, proportions with denominators, odds ratios, or means+SDs)
Completely unrelated to the research topic, or population outside scope (ureteral stones only, paediatric patients, non-randomised designs)
moderators_to_extract: Definition of treatment success used (fully stone-free vs residual fragments =4 mm or other threshold)
Imaging modality used to assess stone-free status (CT vs ultrasound vs plain X-ray)
Mean/median stone size or stone burden category
Stone location within kidney (lower pole vs non-lower pole vs mixed)
Publication type and year (full paper vs conference abstract), country/region, sample size category
effect_size_note: Pool as a random-effects risk ratio of treatment success, ESWL/RIRS, using event counts out of the number randomised (ITT denominators). RR < 1 indicates lower success with ESWL (favours RIRS). Use the trial's own success definition and state it; use the follow-up closest to three months when three months is not reported.
single_outcome_target: treatment success (stone-free rate) at three months
